_comment: Wall-clock seconds for one bats file in its own bats call on a GitHub windows-latest runner, Node 20. Used ONLY to balance CI shards -- never to gate anything. Stale numbers cost balance, never correctness: shard-tests.mjs asserts every file lands in exactly one shard whether or not it appears here.
_why: arc-ci's windows leg costs 1585s against ~145s on ubuntu for the same 563 tests -- 2.82s per test against 0.26s, because every bats `run` spawns a process and windows process creation is dear. Measured 2026-07-31 (run 30611012771): excluding the workspace and bats' binaries from Microsoft Defender changes nothing, because the runner image already ships with realtime protection OFF and both drives excluded. There is no windows-side saving left to find, so the fix stays splitting.
_provenance: 112 of 115 discovered files re-measured in a single pass on 2026-08-12 (run 31627029442, weigh-tests.yml, on feat/arc-bench-slice-06) -- one file per job on windows-latest, each timed in its own bats call with the scanners arc-ci installs, the same method as every earlier pass. Re-run that workflow and paste its block rather than editing numbers by hand. The previous pass (2026-08-10, run 31361908896) measured 104 files; this one closes the gap for the bench files, whose absence had been riding _default_weight and skewing the shard plan.
_evidence: The 2026-08-10 pass measured 104 files, 44 of which had NO entry at all and were riding _default_weight 16. The two this slice grew were among them and wrong in the same direction by roughly sevenfold: leads-journey.bats 111s and leads-mail-guard.bats 120s. (An earlier version of this sentence said 47 covered; 47 was the count MISSING before the run, 44 of them were measured, and the other 3 are the ones _known_gap names.) The method is unchanged from the pass that produced the previous table: one file per job on windows, each timed in its own bats call with the scanners arc-ci installs.
_floor: spine-emit.bats at 160s is the floor no shard count can beat, and design-steel-thread.bats at 156s is second. Both numbers are from the 2026-08-10 pass; the previous prose here quoted 147s and 128s from the 2026-08-03 pass and was left standing when the table under it was replaced -- a measured claim that stops being re-derived starts lying, which is the whole reason this file records provenance. From 12 shards on, the heaviest shard IS that one file, and one file cannot be split.
_known_gap: 3 file(s) measured RED in isolation on windows and are therefore NOT re-weighted from this pass: arc-profile.bats, arc-scan.bats, baseline.bats. Their elapsed time is the time they took to FAIL, which is not the time they take to run. Previous weights retained: arc-profile.bats (kept 39s), arc-scan.bats (kept 58s), baseline.bats (kept 42s). THE RED IS NOT A BENCH REGRESSION AND NOT NEW: the identical three files fail identically in isolation on main (run 31625002487, same day, same method) -- arc-profile 36s, arc-scan 55s, baseline 20s, all rc=1. They PASS in arc-ci only when sharded alongside arc-tools-image.bats, which prepares the arc-tools docker image the semgrep adapter falls back to. That is an UNDECLARED INTER-FILE DEPENDENCY: they pass by shard luck, and any change to the shard plan revokes it. This field exists because an unmeasured entry is a DEFAULT rather than an error (retro-log 2026-08-03); name a new file here rather than letting it disappear. RESOLVED, ledger Phase 00: the four ledger files were named here unmeasured at birth on 2026-08-13 and MEASURED before Phase 00 closed, per-file TAP-span on windows from run 31641578789 (head b65772b, 18/18 selftest jobs green) -- the same method the memory files were weighed by, and the promise that field was written to keep. ledger-money-math.bats 30 tests, shard 11/12, 46.8s, entered 47. ledger-pii-validator.bats 16 tests, 31.4s, entered 31. ledger-parsers.bats 16 tests, 29.8s, entered 30. ledger-determinism.bats 4 tests, 7.3s, entered 7. THE PREDICTION WAS RIGHT AND THE DEFAULT WAS BADLY LOW: money-math is 47s against _default_weight 16, nearly threefold, exactly because each of its tests spawns several arc-event and arc-pnl processes on the leg where process creation dominates. Carrying the default would have under-weighted one windows shard by ~31s on that file alone. CAVEAT ON ledger-determinism: 3 of its 5 tests SKIP without node:sqlite, so 7s is its weight on a Node-20 windows leg and NOT what it costs where the engine-equivalence gate actually runs -- re-measure it if the matrix ever puts Node 22 on windows. All four are TAP spans taken alongside other files rather than a weigh-tests dispatch; re-measure in the next full pass. NAMED-AND-UNMEASURED, ledger Phase 01, 2026-08-13: ledger-ventures-parser.bats and ledger-kill-distance.bats are BORN unmeasured and are riding _default_weight 16 until the first green CI run for this phase produces a TAP span to measure them from -- named here at birth rather than left silent, because an unmeasured entry is a DEFAULT rather than an error and that is precisely how 44 files once rode 16s against real costs up to 123s. The Phase 00 measurement is the reason to expect these to be LOW: every ledger suite measured 30-47s against that same default, and both new files spawn arc-pnl, arc-event and arc-inbox processes per test on the leg where process creation dominates. Measure before Phase 01 closes, by the same TAP-span method recorded above. ledger-close.bats joins them on the same terms, born unmeasured in Phase 02 on 2026-08-13: 21 tests, and it spawns arc-event, arc-pnl, arc-inbox and arc-brief processes per test, which is the shape every ledger suite measured 30-47s for against the default of 16. Three named-and-unmeasured ledger files now ride the default together; measure all three in one pass. MEASURED 2026-08-13 from run 31685435167 (head b529c41, 19/19 jobs green), windows-latest, per-file TAP spans: ledger-ventures-parser.bats 31 tests 60.5s entered 61; ledger-close.bats 21 tests 44.1s entered 44; ledger-kill-distance.bats 20 tests 41.4s entered 41. All three were riding _default_weight 16, so the table was under-counting one windows shard by 130s across them. THE METHOD WAS VALIDATED BEFORE THE NUMBERS WERE WRITTEN: summing every per-test delta in shard 11/12 gives 511.5s against that shard's own whole-run TAP span of 511s, so the spans do not double-count. AND A CONTROL DISAGREED, WHICH IS RECORDED RATHER THAN BURIED: ledger-pii-validator.bats, unchanged at 16 tests, measured 31s in the Phase 00 pass and 73s in this one -- 2.4x, same OS, same runner class, same method. Shard totals also swung (shard 9 ran 385s against a 456s prediction, shard 11 ran 511s against 455s). So THIS TABLE HAS A MUCH WIDER ERROR BAR THAN ITS TWO-DIGIT PRECISION SUGGESTS: it is good enough to stop a 4x under-weight, which is what it exists for, and it is NOT good enough to reason about a 20% difference between two files. Anyone re-deriving a balance from these numbers should treat them as a rank order, not as seconds.
